subject: Hosted API latency measurement artifacts and exception criteria
messages:

Cc: Finora SRE Team <ops@finora.com>

Subject: Clarification: p50/p95 targets vs transient spikes

Hi Stephanie / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — the performance looked promising. Before procurement moves forward we need to lock down how Redwood will measure latency commitments for the hosted API. Specifically:
- How do you handle short-lived spike events that look like p95 breaches but are tied to upstream retries or a noisy client?
- What is your exact measurement window (rolling minute / 5m / hourly buckets) for the p50 and p95 commitments?
- What evidence does Finora need to submit a formal exception request (logs, traces, Kibana links, sample payloads)?

Our procurement team wants a concise exception threshold we can sign off on — we want to avoid open-ended carveouts that would make the SLA meaningless. Can you provide a proposed criteria and a short sample addendum we can share with Legal?

Alex
Alex Turner
Head of SRE, Finora

Finora internal: ops@finora.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Clarification: p50/p95 targets vs transient spikes

Alex — thanks for laying this out. Attaching a draft measurement playbook (measurement_playbook_v1.pdf) and a short proposal below. High-level proposal (TL;DR):

1) Measurement windows
   - p50 measured on a per-request basis with 1-minute rolling sampling aggregated daily (median of request latencies).
   - p95 measured using a 5-minute sliding window sampled at 1s resolution; daily p95 is the 95th percentile across all 5-minute windows in the day.

2) Accepted exception classes (narrow):
   - Planned maintenance windows (must be pre-notified and listed in the dashboard).
   - Provider-region network partitions longer than 2 minutes documented by cloud provider status + at least one customer-facing route failure.
   - Client-side retry storms where the root-cause shows >80% client error rate for 60s across multiple clients (requires client logs).
   - Ingestion spikes exceeding 10x historical 95th percentile sustained >10 minutes (requires capacity and ingress proofs).

3) Evidence required for an exception request:
   - Time-aligned traces (OpenTelemetry) and sample request IDs covering the incident window.
   - Aggregated metrics (per-AZ and per-region) and a 5-minute windowed latency CSV (we provided a sample: latency_evidence_sample.csv).
   - Relevant cloud provider incident IDs or packet capture summaries if available.

4) Review SLA addendum: exceptions are capped to a maximum of 3 discrete exception days per 12-month period without premium remediation credits.

We want to be explicit so Finora's procurement can sign off. If that sounds reasonable I can send a short addendum paragraph for Legal and an impact statement for procurement.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference, Inc.

Adding a technical note on measurement artifacts and cache effects (skeletal):

> On Wed, 25 Apr 2028 at 09:02 Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > 1) Measurement windows
> >    - p50 measured on a per-request basis with 1-minute rolling sampling aggregated daily (median of request latencies).
> >    - p95 measured using a 5-minute sliding window sampled at 1s resolution; daily p95 is the 95th percentile across all 5-minute windows in the day.

Two clarifications to make the measurement repeatable and audit-friendly:
- Sampling resolution: we recommend reserving a 1s sampling resolution for windows where traffic > 200rps to avoid heavy sampling noise at very low QPS.
- KV cache warm-up carveout: initial cold-starts after model version rollouts (first 10 minutes per instance during rollout) are eligible for a narrow cold-start carveout — this must be logged as a deployment rollout event in the customer console and will be limited to at most 5 rollouts/month for standard plans.

Operational steps for an exception review (short):
1. Customer opens exception case in the Console with required evidence.
2. Redwood Ops validates traces + provider incident IDs within 48 hours.
3. If validated, exception day(s) recorded and any remediation credits applied as per contract.

Happy to add this as a bulletized appendix to the playbook.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Product Manager, Performance — Redwood Inference

- We also need a one-paragraph impact statement that explains how the exception caps affect historical credit calculations (how many credits, backstop remediation).

Alex

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finora.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>; Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: p50/p95 targets vs transient spikes

Alex — agreed. Below are two short snippets you can paste into the contract. I’ve attached the playbook + a small sample CSV to show the format we’ll use for evidence. Links to the shared playbook are in the Drive link above.

1) Contract addendum (single paragraph):
"The parties agree that Redwood Inference's latency commitments for Hosted API are defined as follows: p50 is measured as the daily median of per-request latencies sampled at 1-second resolution; p95 is calculated from 5-minute sliding windows sampled at 1-second resolution with the daily p95 defined as the 95th percentile across those windows. Permissible exceptions are limited to: pre-notified maintenance windows, documented cloud provider region/network outages exceeding 2 minutes, verified client-side retry storms with supporting client logs, and ingestion surges >10x baseline sustained >10 minutes. Exceptions will be granted only upon submission of required evidence (time-aligned traces, per-region metrics, and provider incident IDs) and are capped at three discrete exception days per 12-month period unless otherwise agreed in writing."

2) Procurement impact statement (one paragraph):
"The exception cap limits the total days in which Redwood will waive latency credit calculations to three discrete calendar days per rolling 12-month period. For any validated exception day, Redwood will not apply standard SLA credits; instead, the parties will engage remediation playbooks and, where capacity-related exceptions occur, Redwood will provide prioritized capacity remediation and a single remediation credit equal to 5% of the monthly hosted API spend for the month in which the exception is validated. The capped-exception model reduces exposure to open-ended SLA carveouts while providing a predictable remediation and credit mechanism for the customer."

Next steps: Ben, Laura — can you drop a version of the clause into the standard addendum template and route to Finora Legal? Alex — once procurement confirms the wording I’ll prepare the formal amendment and we can schedule a quick legal call if needed.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
